statement: Let M = 1000000007. For a supplier j < len(boxes), call j feasible if for every i < len(packages) there is k < len(boxes[j]) with packages[i] <= boxes[j][k]. For a feasible j, let Waste(j) be the minimum, over all functions a from {0,...,len(packages)-1} to {0,...,len(boxes[j])-1} satisfying packages[i] <= boxes[j][a(i)] for every i, of sum_{i=0}^{len(packages)-1} (boxes[j][a(i)] - packages[i]); the same box size may be reused any number of times. Whenever the function returns a result r, if no supplier is feasible then r = -1; otherwise, letting W = min{ Waste(j) | j < len(boxes) and j is feasible }, we have 0 <= r < M and r is congruent to W modulo M.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, let W be the exact minimum total waste over all feasible suppliers, where a supplier is feasible if every package fits some box of that supplier, and waste for a supplier is minimized using only that supplier's box sizes with unlimited reuse. Then W = 0 if and only if there exists a supplier j < len(boxes) such that for every package i < len(packages) there is an index k < len(boxes[j]) with boxes[j][k] = packages[i]. In particular, if such a supplier exists then r = 0.

Consequently, if some supplier is feasible, W = min{ sum_{i=0}^{len(packages)-1} (min{ boxes[j][k] | k < len(boxes[j]) and boxes[j][k] >= packages[i] } - packages[i]) | j < len(boxes) and j is feasible }, and r = W mod 1000000007. For a fixed supplier, the minimum is attained by assigning each package independently to the smallest box size of that supplier that is at least the package; unlimited supply makes the choices independent.
